by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

question.population: Adults, healthy or with an illness

decisions.reason: Pools RCTs of CoQ10 versus placebo or standard treatment with fatigue as an outcome, but only in people with depression, a narrower group.
Pools 13 RCTs of CoQ10 versus placebo for fatigue in healthy and ill participants, with a separate CoQ10-only subgroup.

question.population: Adults taking statins, most with muscle symptoms

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 versus a control group in adults on statins, with muscle pain intensity as the outcome.
Looks at CoQ10 for exercise-induced muscle damage and oxidative stress, not in people taking statins.
Looks at athletes and exercise-related blood markers, not adults on statins with muscle pain.
Covers exercise-induced muscle damage markers and physical performance in adults generally, not statin users.
Pooled RCTs of oral CoQ10 versus placebo in patients with statin-induced myopathy, with a muscle pain analysis.
Pooled RCTs of oral CoQ10 versus placebo in adults with statin-associated myalgia, with muscle pain as the outcome.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 versus placebo in statin-induced myopathy, reporting muscle pain and other muscle symptoms.
Measures how statins affect blood CoQ10 levels; it does not test CoQ10 supplements for muscle pain.
Measures how statins affect plasma CoQ10 levels; it does not test CoQ10 supplements for muscle pain.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 versus control in statin-treated patients, with a muscle pain analysis.
Studies CoQ10 for physical capacity and muscle function in middle-aged and older adults, not muscle pain in people taking statins.
Includes RCTs of oral CoQ10 versus placebo in adults with statin-associated myalgia, with statin muscle symptoms as the outcome.
Covers statin users and CoQ10 but mostly looks at blood CoQ10 levels in a broad literature search, with little trial data on muscle symptoms.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 vs control on blood pressure, but in people with cardiometabolic disorders in general rather than specifically hypertension.
Included RCTs of CoQ10 in older adults with hypertension or CVD, but added to usual therapy, mixed population, and results were not pooled.
Pooled double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs of CoQ10 on blood pressure in adults with primary hypertension.
Pooled double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs of CoQ10 on blood pressure in patients with primary hypertension.
Summarised eight CoQ10 trials in hypertension, but the abstract does not say they were randomised or placebo-controlled.
Broad narrative review of many nutraceuticals for blood pressure; CoQ10 is mentioned but not pooled in its own analysis.
Separate analysis of randomised placebo-controlled trials of CoQ10 on blood pressure in hypertensive patients.
Pools RCTs of CoQ10 on blood pressure, but in adults in general; the abstract reports no separate analysis of people with high blood pressure.
Pooled RCTs of oral CoQ10 around exercise and included maximal oxygen uptake, a performance outcome, alongside blood markers.
CoQ10 trials in athletes, but outcomes were only blood markers of oxidative stress and muscle damage, not exercise performance.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 in adults with physical performance as an outcome, alongside muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.
Population was COPD patients, and CoQ10 was mainly tested combined with creatine; this is a different question from healthy adults.
Pools randomised trials of oral CoQ10 in athletes only, a narrower group; mainly oxidative stress markers, with VO2max as the only performance outcome; comparator not stated.
Pools randomised trials comparing CoQ10 with placebo in healthy adults, with exercise performance as an outcome.

question.outcome: How often attacks happen and how bad they are

decisions.reason: Network meta-analysis of RCTs in adult migraineurs that gives a CoQ10 vs placebo estimate for attack frequency and severity.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 vs placebo for prophylaxis in adults with migraine, reporting attack frequency and severity; combined-supplement use was analysed as a subgroup.
Dose-response meta-analysis of RCTs that reports a separate CoQ10 vs control analysis for migraine prevention, with frequency and severity outcomes and adult comparisons.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 for migraine, reporting attack frequency and severity; the abstract does not say whether patients were adults or what the comparator was.
CoQ10 vs placebo for migraine attacks and severity matches, but the pooled trials mix children and adults with no separate adult-only analysis.

question.population: Adults with heart failure on standard treatment
question.outcome: Deaths, hospital stays or heart function

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 added to heart failure treatment, reporting all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalisation and ejection fraction.
Cochrane meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CoQ10 with placebo or conventional therapy in people with heart failure, assessing efficacy and safety.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 plus standard care versus standard care with mortality data, but only in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, a narrower group.
Covers ubiquinol and ejection fraction in heart failure RCTs, but it is a broad review of many supplements with no pooled CoQ10 analysis described.
Evidence map that pooled RCTs of CoQ10 in heart failure patients and reports a risk ratio for all-cause mortality.
Cochrane review of RCTs of CoQ10 in heart failure patients, with meta-analysis of beneficial and harmful effects where data allowed.
Meta-analysis of RCTs of CoQ10 in chronic heart failure, measuring ejection fraction and cardiac output (heart function).
Includes a separate meta-analysis of RCTs of CoQ10 in heart failure that looked at ejection fraction and mortality.
Meta-analyses of placebo-controlled RCTs of add-on CoQ10 in congestive heart failure, measuring ejection fraction and cardiac output.
CoQ10 in heart failure matches, but the review covers only people with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), a narrower group; no abstract to confirm comparison or outcomes.

question.population: Adults, often with diabetes or other metabolic conditions
question.outcome: HbA1c, blood sugar, cholesterol or triglycerides

decisions.reason: CoQ10 and glucose/HbA1c outcomes match, but this umbrella review pooled earlier meta-analyses rather than the randomised trials themselves.
Pooled RCTs of oral CoQ10 vs placebo in adults with and without T2DM, reporting fasting glucose and HbA1c.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 in people with prediabetes and T2DM, reporting triglycerides, fasting blood sugar and lipid profile.
Pooled 64 RCTs of CoQ10 in metabolic disorders, reporting triglycerides, cholesterol, HbA1c and fasting glucose.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 in adults with type 2 diabetes, reporting cholesterol and triglycerides.
Pooled 50 RCTs of CoQ10 in adults, reporting total cholesterol, LDL, HDL and triglycerides.
Outcomes are oxidative stress markers, not blood sugar, HbA1c or blood lipids.
Pooled RCTs in T2DM with a separate CoQ10 analysis (as an add-on to diabetes drugs) for HbA1c and fasting glucose.
Narrower group (diabetic kidney disease), CoQ10 given with other medicines, and only 4 RCTs mixed with experimental studies.
CoQ10 vs placebo on lipids, but in a narrower group (women with PCOS) within a network meta-analysis of supplements.
CoQ10 vs placebo on glucose and lipids, but only in women with PCOS, within a network meta-analysis.
Outcome is blood pressure only, not blood sugar, HbA1c or lipids.
Pooled controlled trials of CoQ10 in metabolic diseases, reporting triglycerides and cholesterol.
CoQ10 vs placebo on lipids, but the people had coronary artery disease rather than diabetes or metabolic conditions.
CoQ10 RCTs reporting lipids and fasting glucose, but in a different group: people with chronic kidney disease.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 vs control; main outcome Lp(a), but total cholesterol and triglycerides were also pooled.
Pooled placebo-controlled RCTs of CoQ10, reporting blood glucose and HbA1c in people with and without high glucose.
Pooled placebo-controlled RCTs of CoQ10 in diabetes, with a CoQ10-alone analysis of glucose control and lipids.
CoQ10 vs placebo in metabolic syndrome, but main outcomes are adipokines and inflammation; glucose control only mentioned in passing.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 vs control, reporting fasting blood glucose and HbA1c.
Pooled RCTs on lipids and glucose, but CoQ10 was only given within a combination with red yeast rice, berberine, policosanol and other ingredients.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 in adults with NAFLD, a metabolic condition, and reported cholesterol and triglyceride outcomes.
Pooled 40 RCTs of CoQ10 and reported fasting glucose and HbA1c, with greater effects shown in people with diabetes.
This is a letter to the editor, not a systematic review that pools trials.
This is a reply to a letter to the editor, not a systematic review that pools trials.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 against placebo in people with diabetes or metabolic syndrome, reporting cholesterol and metabolic markers.
Pooled RCTs of CoQ10 against placebo or other drugs in type 2 diabetes, reporting HbA1c, fasting glucose, TG and HDL.
This is a commentary on a review about blood pressure, not a pooled review of glucose or lipid outcomes.
Covers mixed antioxidants for diabetic retinopathy with no pooling, and its outcomes are eye disease and oxidative markers.
